Here, we report a hydroacridine-based fluorophore that addresses the often encountered limitations by providing caging-group-free activation using visible light.

title: Chiral Intramolecular Ether–Borane FLPs for Asymmetric Ketone Hydrogenation
abstract: Asymmetric hydrogenation of ketones remains challenging in frustrated Lewis pair (FLP) catalysis, largely because the low basicity of ketones places stringent demands on both H 2 activation and stereocontrol. Here we introduce binaphthyl ether–boranes (BINEBs), a new class of chiral intramolecular FLPs featuring a bis-ether Lewis base tethered to a strongly Lewis acidic borane on an axially chiral binaphthyl scaffold. BINEBs catalyze the asymmetric hydrogenation of a broad range of aromatic ketones, delivering chiral secondary alcohols with high enantioselectivities.

title: Herzberg–Teller eﬀect as a phonon-assisted optical transition in molecules
abstract: This study derives expressions for the photophysics of a molecule exhibiting the Herzberg–Teller (HT) effect. The derivation is based on Fermi’s golden rule, and the Longuet-Higgins representation, where the electron–photon and vibronic couplings are treated as perturbations, is used. All the vibrational modes are included, thus enabling the assignment of vibronic progressions in the spectrum originating from Franck–Condon factors.

title: Thioalkyltetrazines Synthesis from Aldehyde Precursors and Application in Ag-Mediated Liebeskind-Srogl Coupling
abstract: Tetrahydrotetrazines are readily prepared from aldehydes, but have minimal precedent as precursors to tetrazines of value to bioorthogonal chemistry applications. Formaldehyde and glyoxylate esters undergo condensation with ([1,1'-biphenyl]-4-ylmethyl)thiocarbohydrazide bromide to give practical access to new thioalkyltetrazines as crystalline solids. 3-(([1,1’-biphenyl]-4-ylmethyl)thio)-tetrazine (h-Tz) was used for the synthesis of monosubstituted tetrazines via silver-mediated Liebeskind-Srogl coupling.

title: Extending Hertzian Contact Area Theory to Plastic Deformation of Glassy Polymer Particles
abstract: Quantifying the mechanical response of polymer particles under compression is fundamentally hindered by a deceptively simple problem: the contact area between the particle and compression plate can rarely be directly measured during deformation. Since Hertz formulated his contact theory in 1881, widely used Hertzian and adhesive contact models have remained largely confined to the elastic regime, leaving the plastic deformation behavior of polymer particles fundamentally out of reach.

title: A Silica-Supported Tungsten-Iridium Hydride Catalyst with Enhanced Arene H/D Exchange performances
abstract: Despite extensive exploration of reaction conditions, the direct synthesis of a molecular tungsten-iridium complex from Cp*IrH 4 and W(≡C t Bu)(Np) 3 remained elusive. However, we discovered that the silica-supported tungsten alkylidyne species, (≡SiO)W(≡C t Bu)(CH 2 t Bu) 2 , readily reacts with Cp*IrH 4 , enabling the formation of heterobimetallic surface species, (≡SiO)W(CH 2 t Bu) 2 (H) n IrCp*.

title: Synthesis and Reactivity of Fluorene-Bridged Cyclic Diaryliodonium Salts
abstract: Spirocyclic organic compounds play a significant role in organic materials, particularly in the field of optoelectronics. In this study, novel spiro-bridged cyclic diaryliodonium salts were synthesised in yields of up to 78%. The structure of the parent salt was confirmed by X-ray crystallography, and the salt was functionalised in iodine-chalcogen exchanges towards highly valuable xanthene derivatives in up to 88% yield.

title: Isolation and bonding analysis of copper(I)-xenon complex stabilized by weakly coordinating alkoxyaluminate anion.
abstract: The first crystalline Cu(I)-Xe complex, Xe-Cu[Al(OR F ) 4 ], 1 , (R F = C(CF 3 ) 3 ), forms as a salt of the weakly coordinating perfluorinated alkoxyaluminate upon ligand exchange between elemental xenon and Cu(I)-N 2 complex, Cu(N 2 )[Al(OR F ) 4 ]. Despite the lack of relativistic character of the copper ion, 1 is obtained under ambient Xe pressure and at room temperature. The crystal structure reveals that it is a molecular compound where xenon is a terminal ligand to copper with steric factors causing a Cu-Xe bond elongation in comparison with known gas-phase Xe-Cu(I) species.

title: High-resolution mass spectrometry revealed that amino acid-based surfactants as a potential contributor to bacterial regrowth in tap water
abstract: Microbial regrowth in tap water poses a potential threat to public health. Although biodegradable organic matter (BOM) supports microbial proliferation, specific BOM components remain largely unknown. This study evaluated the bacterial growth potential and explored BOM components in tap water samples collected from a hospital and a university. In the hospital sample, indigenous microbial communities grew up to 107 cells/mL after several days of incubation. Amplicon sequencing revealed that abundance of Methylotenera mobilis increased significantly.

title: A Framework for Quantifying and Attributing Molecular Standardization Reproducibility in Cheminformatics Pipelines
abstract: Molecular structure standardization, which normalizes salts, charge states, tautomers, isotopes and stereochemistry to a canonical form, is mandatory in essentially every cheminformatics pipeline. The protocols used to perform it nonetheless vary across tools, databases and configurations. Disagreement between standardization pipelines is documented at production scale, but existing analyses compare one pipeline against one reference, so they cannot identify which normalization decision produced a given disagreement.

title: A Blood–Brain Barrier-on-Chip Approaching In Vivo Tightness for Quantitative Ultrasound-Mediated Opening
abstract: The blood–brain barrier (BBB) remains one of the greatest obstacles to the treatment of neurological diseases, preventing the delivery of nearly all large therapeutics and most small molecules to the brain. Although ultrasound-activated microbubbles offer a promising strategy for transient BBB opening, quantitative in vitro models capable of reproducing physiological barrier properties while allowing controlled ultrasound studies remain scarce.

title: Motional Mode Conversion in the Orbitrap
abstract: Resonant coupling between motional modes has played an important role in trapped-ion physics and Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance (FTICR) mass spectrometry, enabling ion manipulation, cooling, centering, and precision measurements. In contrast, controlled mode conversion in the Orbitrap mass analyzer has received little attention. Here we develop a general theory of motional mode conversion in the Orbitrap and identify three classes of resonant transfer: radial-axial (), azimuthal-axial (), and radial-azimuthal () conversion.

title: When Philicity Fails: Mechanistic Control of Ambiphilic Metal–Superoxo Reactivity
abstract: A fundamental challenge in oxygen activation chemistry is understanding the factors that govern the switch between electrophilic and nucleophilic reactivity in metal–superoxo intermediates. Notably, only four ambiphilic metal–superoxo systems have been reported to date, yet the origins of their ambiphilic behavior remain poorly understood, limiting the rational design of catalysts with predictable and tunable reactivity.

title: Light-Driven Dissolution of Ultrasmall Maghemite Nanoparticles: The Role of Ligand and Photon Energy
abstract: Light-controlled conversion of iron oxide nanoparticles into redox-active soluble iron offers a route toward externally triggered, image-guided ferroptosis strategies, but the physicochemical factors governing this process remain poorly understood. Here, visible-light-driven dissolution of ultrasmall citrate-stabilized maghemite nanoparticles (3.4 ± 0.8 nm) is shown to arise from a competition between iron release and nanoparticle aggregation. The process involves iron oxide reduction, ferrous iron release, citrate detachment and oxidation, and subsequent nanoparticle aggregation.

title: A review on foundation models for polymer informatics
abstract: Foundation models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for learning transferable knowledge from broad, heterogeneous data and adapting them to diverse downstream tasks, driving a growing interest in AI-accelerated scientific discovery. In polymer science, this paradigm offers a promising route beyond conventional machine learning methods that are often confined to isolated tasks and struggle to generalize under data scarcity and across heterogeneous downstream settings. Polymer foundation models (PFMs), however, are not merely general scientific foundation models applied to polymer datasets.

title: Dynamic Flow Experimentation for Data-Rich Polymer Synthesis
abstract: Growing global challenges in healthcare, energy, sustainability, and technology have motivated increased automation and robotics to accelerate material discovery and development. Continuous droplet flow chemistry has provided a solution to non-uniform mixing and transport phenomena and provides the advantages of batch reactions for screening individual reaction conditions and reagent compositions.

title: Super-Reaction Enhancement of Polariton-Mediated Electron Transfer
abstract: We investigate the enhancement of polariton-mediated electron transfer (PMET) using a general super-reaction mechanism where multiple donor sites locally couple to individual acceptors. We demonstrate that this enhancement extends to the collective light-matter coupling regime with a large number of acceptors and cavity-coupled donors. We use analytic rate theory and quantum dynamics simulations to show that the local super-reaction mechanism serves as an additional enhancement to the delocalized driving force enhancement of PMET.

title: Basis-Set Limit Wavefunction Energies of Massive Water Clusters: Resolution of a Challenge for Many-Body Expansion
abstract: The many-body expansion (MBE) offers a route to high-level wavefunction energies of systems beyond the reach of conventional calculations, but its practical convergence is entangled with basis set superposition error (BSSE), electrostatic embedding, and the scarcity of direct supersystem benchmarks at large size. Here, we show that as the complete-basis-set (CBS) limit is approached, electrostatically embedded three-body MBE, EE-MBE(3), provides accurate absolute and relative HF, RI-MP2, and CCSD(T) energies across water clusters of varying sizes.

title: High-Resolution 3D Laser Printing of Microalgae-Derived Materials for Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers localized, controllable cancer treatment through reactive oxygen species (ROS) generated by light-activated photosensitizers. Three-dimensional (3D) printing of PDT-active materials has emerged as a powerful tool for fabricating customized structures with controlled architecture and composition. However, conventional PDT materials often require complex, multi-step syntheses with low yields. Consequently, integrating natural photosensitizers into biocompatible matrices represents a crucial step towards sustainable PDT.

title: A Charge-Directed Electrocyclic Ring Opening of Azomethine Ylides as a Route to 2-(N-Acylamino)-1,3-dienes
abstract: The electrocyclic ring opening of azomethine ylides driven by charge neutralization leads to 2-N-acylamino-1,3-diene products. The requisite azomethine ylide is formed by deprotonation of an oxazolinium ion, which is formed by O-silylation of a readily available oxazolidinone starting material. Computational studies indicate that the deprotonation event is the rate limiting step of the sequence providing a short-lived ylide intermediate that opens spontaneously via a low-barrier (1.7 kcal/mol) transition state leading to an enecarbamate product that is about 48 kcal/mol lower in energy than…

title: Correlative Potential and Impedance Microscopy Reveals Particle-Level Degradation and Transport Heterogeneity in Solid-State Composite Cathodes
abstract: The electrochemical performance of composite cathodes in all-solid-state batteries is governed by local reaction and transport processes; however, directly linking cell-level electrochemical responses to individual activematerial particles and local microstructural features remains challenging. Here, we investigate a composite cathode in sulfide-based all-solid-state cells using correlative microscopy combining Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) and scanning impedance microscopy (SIM).

title: Excitonic Coupling Suppresses Phonon-Induced Polariton Group Velocity Renormalization
abstract: Exciton-polaritons can transport electronic excitation energy ballistically over distances far exceeding those accessible to bare excitons, yet their measured group velocities are often substantially lower than those predicted from the bare polariton dispersion. Recent experiments have shown that excitonic transfer coupling of the materials coupled inside the cavity can reduce the magnitude of group velocity renormalization, even though it does not impact the measured optical dispersion relation of polaritons.

title: Growth and crystallization of solution-processed TIPSpentacene on ultra-thin ferroelectric HZO gate dielectrics
abstract: The solution processed organic thin film growth on the ferroelectric Hf0.5Zr0.5O2(HZO) thin films was investigated using the most commonly used TIPS-pentacene toward memory device applications. The molecular orientations, surface morphologies, and crystallinity of TIPS pentacene deposited on HZO were comparable to those of fabricated thin films on SiO2. In particular, 2D-GIXD results showed that TIPS-pentacene on HZO crystallized by annealing at 150°C exhibited higher crystallinity and molecular orientation than that on SiO2.

title: N-aminated N-heterocycle based hydrazones as widely tunable photoswitches
abstract: Photoswitches based on E/Z isomerism around a C=N bond have found wide-reaching applications in materials science and biology. Herein, we report a new class of hydrazone photoswitch based on aminated nitrogen heterocycles, the N-aminated N-heterocyclic hydrazones (NaNs). These photoswitches can be synthesised in a single step, achieve near quantitative photoswitching, offer visible light (470 nm) response, have thermal half-lives of up to 958 hours at room temperature and quantum yields of up to 70%.

title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations of the Outer-Sphere Reorganization Energies of Aqueous Oligothiophenes
abstract: The outer-sphere reorganization energy (λout) contributes directly to the activation barrier for hole transfer in aqueous organic mixed ionic–electronic conductors, yet it is usually estimated from dielectric continuum models rather than computed explicitly. Here, λout is computed for doped oligothiophenes in explicit aqueous electrolyte by all-atom molecular dynamics with an electronic continuum correction, using vertical-energy-gap fluctuation estimators and thermodynamic integration.

title: Checkmate for CHK2: Discovery of First-in-Class Covalent CHK2 Inhibitors with High Potency and Selectivity
abstract: Checkpoint kinase 2 (CHK2), a serine/threonine kinase encoded by CHEK2, plays a key role in the DNA damage response (DDR), acting downstream of ataxia-telangiectasia mutated (ATM) kinase in the ATM–CHK2–p53 signaling axis. Despite considerable interest in CHK2 as a potential therapeutic target, our understanding of its biological functions and therapeutic potential remains constrained by the limited availability of potent and selective chemical probes.

title: Sulfilimine benziodoxolones: stable electrophilic bifunctional reagents for nitrogen incorporation
abstract: We report the design and scalable synthesis of novel sulfilimine-based hypervalent iodine reagents (INSert, based on the I-N=S motif), that are bench-stable, non-explosive and can act as bifunctional electrophilic nitrogen donors. Their distinctive architecture combines a benziodoxolone moiety to induce electrophilicity at the nitrogen atom, with a sulfilimine group as a versatile, latent synthetic handle for downstream diversification.

title: Spatially programmed MOF-coated microchannels for capillary-driven microvolume analysis
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer chemically and geometrically programmable pore environments that have been exploited as coatings for capillary- and fiber-based microextraction. However, most formats still rely on discrete adsorbent handling or external fluid actuation, poorly suited to the microliter sample volumes typical of biological specimens.

title: Analytic Nuclear Gradients and Derivative Couplings for SA-QED-CASSCF
abstract: Exploring the potential energy surfaces of molecules in optical cavities requires analytical derivatives. We present analytical nuclear gradients and nonadiabatic derivative couplings for state-averaged quantum-electrodynamics complete-active-space self-consistent field theory (SA-QED-CASSCF) forthe coherent-state Pauli–Fierz Hamiltonian, including the coupledperturbed response of the QED-Hartree–Fock reference and the photon contribution to the coupling that arises because the coherent-state displacement depends on the geometry.

title: Probing local structure and hydrogen incorporation in solution-processed thin-film solid electrolytes
abstract: Solution processing of functional thin films offers significant benefits, yet characterising their local structure and bulk composition remains challenging. Here, we investigate the composition-structure-property relationships of nanocomposite Na-Al-P-O (NAPO) thin-film solid electrolytes using impedance spectroscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy and time-of-flight elastic recoil detection analysis (ToF-ERDA).

title: Small-Angle X-ray Scattering and Rheology Reveal the Onset of Interparticle Correlations during Nanoparticle Immobilization in Polystyrene
abstract: The immobilization of nanoparticles in polymer matrices is a key strategy to suppress Brownian motion while preserving nanoparticle functionality. In this work, monodisperse iron oxide nanoparticles with mean diameters of 6.4, 7.1, and 8.8 nm were synthesized via thermal decomposition of an iron–oleate complex and immobilized in a styrene matrix by radical polymerization. TEM and SAXS confirm that particle size and morphology remain unchanged, whereas interparticle correlations and larger-scale clusters develop during immobilization.

title: Resolving Water-Oxidation Kinetics by Combining Operando Spectroscopy with O2 Evolution Rates over Seven Orders of Magnitude
abstract: Electrocatalytic water oxidation is central to renewable energy conversion, yet the origin of its potential–current response remains challenging to define. Classical electrode kinetics attributes the empirical exponential increase in current with potential to the linearly lowering of the activation barrier with applied potential, as described by Butler–Volmer formalisms, while potential-dependent coverage of active surface states has also been considered as an important factor in electrocatalytic kinetics.

title: Photonic neuromorphic learning via generalized in situ physical gradient descent
Overcoming the Density Limitation of Polyhydroxyurethane Self-Blown Foams through Sol–Gel Chemistry
abstract: Non-isocyanate polyurethane foams (NIPUFs), particularly polyhydroxyurethane (PHU) foams prepared by cyclic carbonate aminolysis, are promising safer alternatives to conventional polyurethane foams. Although water-induced CO 2 self-blowing can now be achieved from room-temperature formulations within minutes, access to foams with densities below 150 kg·m -3 remains a significant challenge. Herein, we introduce alkoxysilanes as additives for the fabrication of NIPUFs with ultra-low densities (30–50 kg·m -3 ).

title: Lookahead Bayesian Optimisation for Molecular Growth in Self-Driving Laboratories
abstract: Self-driving laboratories can autonomously execute iterative design-make-test-analyse cycles, but molecular optimisation presents a distinctive challenge: selecting which compound to elaborate determines not only the next experiment, but also the chemical space accessible in subsequent rounds. Conventional molecular Bayesian optimisation typically evaluates compounds without considering how their selection changes what can subsequently be synthesised.

title: Spin-dependent thermoelectric transportproperties of DPH-based molecular device
DNA binders based on the integration of duocarmycins into minor groove-targeting polyamides have potent and selective anti-trypansosomal activity
abstract: Duocarmycins are attractive DNA alkylating agents due to their high potency; however, increasing their selectivity has always been a challenge. Here, we describe the integration of the duocarmycin subunits DSA and CI into minor groove-targeting polyamides, compounds that can ‘read’ DNA sequences. The synthesis of a CI analogue suitably substituted for solid phase synthesis using Fmoc-chemistry is described. The synthesis of the hybrid compounds is achieved using solid phase methods on chloro-trityl resin.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Aquatic Ecotoxicity Prediction
abstract: Aquatic ecosystems are threatened by thousands of chemicals whose hazard is often unknown. Laboratory tests of individual chemicals on individual species establish, for example, the Lethal Concentration for 50% of test individuals (LC50), but for most chemicals in use such data exist for only a small fraction of species. A growing body of research applies machine learning to bridge these gaps. Before such models can be relied on in regulatory and environmental management contexts, they must not only be accurate in general, but also quantify how far individual predictions can be trusted.

title: A field-deployable method for measuring picomolar mercury levels in natural waters
abstract: Measurements of mercury (Hg) at sub- to picomolar concentrations in natural waters often rely on cold vapor atomic fluorescence spectrometry (CVAFS), which provides the sensitivity required for trace detection. However, CVAFS instruments are not well suited for routine field deployment and require compressed high-purity argon or helium gas to operate, limiting their use in remote regions and locations without established analytical infrastructure.

title: Fourteen-Membered Macrocyclic Copper Complex for Highly Selective Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction to Ammonia
abstract: The selective electrochemical reduction of nitrate (NO3−) to ammonia (NH3) represents a promising route for sustainable NH3 production. However, achieving high NH3 selectivity remains challenging due to competing reactions. Additionally, many reported catalysts rely on noble metals and often require relatively elevated catalyst loadings to achieve high apparent activity, while most systems operate only at relatively low current densities.

title: Additive Manufacturing of Polyvinylidene Fluoride (PVDF) Toward High Performance with AI-Driven Workflows
abstract: Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a high-performance fluoropolymer known for its chemical resistance, mechanical strength, thermal stability, and piezoelectric and dielectric behavior, making it an ideal material for additive manufacturing (AM). The first part of this paper provides an overview and demonstration of this potential, with the first section reviewing PVDF materials, crystallographic phases, and fused deposition modeling (FDM) processing.

title: Hydrogen-Assisted Reduction of Metal Oxides: Reaction Mechanisms, Process Optimization, and AI/ML-Enabled Pathways for Sustainable Materials Processing
abstract: Hydrogen reduction of metal oxides has been identified as a promising approach for producing some engineering (metallic) materials, both through primary production and the reprocessing of waste materials. Such an approach offers a viable promise for the production of value-added materials in a sustainable manner. Unlike in other reduction processes, where obnoxious gases get 2 released as byproducts, hydrogen reduction, on the other hand, generate water vapor as the clean principal byproduct.

title: Deoxygenative Dialkylation of Vinylic Epoxides to Chiral Alkanes by Double SN2’
abstract: Chiral alkanes bearing two contiguous tertiary all-carbon stereocentres are important motifs in bioactive molecules, natural products and functional compounds, yet their stereocontrolled synthesis remains challenging. Here we report their modular preparation through the formal deoxygenative dialkylation of enantioenriched vinyl epoxides. Two consecutive organocopper-mediated S N 2′ substitutions enable stereospecific transfer of the starting stereochemical information followed by diastereoselective installation of the adjacent stereocentre.

title: Energy ordering of singlet and triplet excitedstates in s-indacene, Pentalene,Cyclobutadiene derivatives in singlet fission : A model exact and density matrixrenormalization group study
A bipartite quantum-acoustic architecture stabilizes multi-exciton solitons at 323 K
Fusion-Number-Dependent Emergence of 16π-Electron Antiaromatic Circuits in Thienocyclopenta-Fused Pyrenes
abstract: Antiaromatic 4nπ-electron circuits provide a powerful strategy for narrowing the HOMO–LUMO gaps of π-conjugated molecules, yet their contribution is often attenuated or obscured in stable polycyclic frameworks by competing local aromatic stabilization. Here we report a systematic series of thienocyclopenta-fused pyrenes containing one ( 1TP ), two ( trans -2TP and cis -2TP ), or four ( 4TP ) fused thienocyclopentadiene units, designed to evaluate the stepwise contributions of embedded 16π-electron circuits.

title: Pore-network homogeneity for mechanically reliable powder-compacted solid-electrolyte separators
abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) with alloy anodes require solid-electrolyte (SE) separators that sustain ion transport while accommodating repeated electrode-derived mechanical loads. However, the mechanical state of powder-compacted separators is commonly inferred from bulk porosity, averaged mechanical properties, or cell-level stack pressure changes, obscuring spatially heterogeneous local responses.

title: pH-responsive nanopores enable programmable transmembrane potential
abstract: Biological ion channels achieve highly selective, ultrafast ion transport through stimulus-responsive gating, in which conformational changes triggered by chemical cues such as pH that modulate channel permeability with exquisite precision. Replicating this coupled chemical-structural functionality in synthetic membranes remains a fundamental challenge, particularly for scalable platforms relevant to energy harvesting, desalination, and chemical sensing.

title: A quantitative roadmap from catalyst benchmarks to commercial hybrid electrolysis
abstract: Hybrid water electrolysis replaces the sluggish oxygen evolution reaction with the oxidation of an organic substrate, producing hydrogen alongside another value-added chemical. In its most efficient form, the electrochemical oxidative dehydrogenation (EOD) of aldehydes, hydrogen evolves at both electrodes with specific electricity consumption down to 4 kWh kg−1 totalH2 , tenfold lower than conventional water electrolysis.

title: Substituent-Controlled Divergent Photocyclization of Aza-1,5 Dienes to Access Three Distinct Cyclic Frameworks
abstract: Rigid, three-dimensional cyclic scaffolds are highly valued in medicinal chemistry, yet selectively accessing dis tinct cyclic frameworks from a common class of simple acyclic precursors remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a precious-metal-free photochemical cyclization of aza-1,5-dienes that enables the substituent-controlled, divergent synthe sis of three distinct cyclic frameworks: bridged bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes, fused bicyclo[2.2.0]hexanes, and six-membered lac tams.

title: Phase-Controlled Efficient Nitrate-to-Dinitrogen Electroreduction on an α-Co/NC@CNT Electrified Membrane Platform
abstract: Selective electrochemical conversion of nitrate (NO 3 - ) to dinitrogen (N 2 ) is attractive for nitrate remediation but remains challenging because competing hydrogenation pathways often yield reduced nitrogen products. Here, we develop a self-supported flexible electrified membrane (α-Co/NC@CNTFEM) by integrating phase-defined hexagonal close-packed (HCP) α-Co/nitrogen-doped carbon (NC) into a conductive carbon nanotube (CNT) framework.

title: Effects of Zinc Leachate on the Structure and Activity of Semaglutide
abstract: Semaglutide is among the most prescribed Glucagon-like peptide-1 agonists (GLP-1As) for treatment of type II diabetes and obesity in both oral (Rybelsus®, Wegovy®) and injectable (Ozempic®, Wegovy®) formulations. Injectable semaglutide is often manufactured in prefilled syringes, which facilitate convenient storage and independent dosage for patients. Recently, potential leaching of zinc from the elastomer of the inner needle shield has been evaluated for pharmaceutical antibody formulations. The leached zinc ion may impose a risk of drug aggregation, particle formation, and needle clogging.

title: Photoresponsive Dynamics in HABI-Carbamate-Silsesquioxane Hybrid Polymer Networks with Tunable Thermomechanical Properties and Shape-Memory Behaviors
abstract: Photoresponsive polymer networks that reversibly modulate their mechanical properties under light irradiation are promising materials for advanced actuators and shape-memory systems. Herein, we report the synthesis of a new family of hexaarylbiimidazole (HABI)-carbamate-siloxane hybrid polymer networks containing methyl, phenyl, vinyl, acrylate, methacrylate, and isooctyl organotrialkoxysilane structures. The polymers were prepared through simultaneous urethane formation and siloxane condensation.

title: Consecutive hydrodefluorination for the regioselective synthesis of partially fluorinated arenes
abstract: Fluorinated arenes are critically important motifs in drug discovery, often exhibiting superior bioactivity compared to their non-fluorinated counterparts. While advances in fluorination methods have improved access to monofluoroarenes, the synthesis of di- and trifluoroarenes remains challenging. Here, we present a powerful method for access to partially fluorinated arenes via consecutive hydrodefluorination of perfluoroarenes, executed in one ‘pot’.

title: Bonding, Biradicaloid Character, and Real-Space Topology of the Dinitrosyl Beryllium Dimer Be2(NO)2: A Multiconfigurational and Energy-Decomposition Study
abstract: The structural, vibrational, thermodynamic, multiconfigurational electronic structure, biradicaloid character, charge-transfer bonding, and real-space topological properties of the dinitrosyl beryllium dimer, Be2(NO)2, are investigated using density functional theory (DFT) at the TPSS/def2-TZVP-D4 level, complete active space self-consistent field (CASSCF) coupled with N-electron valence state second-order perturbation theory (NEVPT2), STEOM-DLPNO-CCSD, and multi-wavefunction topological analyses via Multiwfn.

title: Stereochemical Control of Static Strength and Dynamic Fracture for Efficient Atomization of Supramolecular Gel Propellants
abstract: Supramolecular gel propellants immobilize liquid fuels through the efficient self-assembly of low-molecular-weight gelators, enabling storage-stable networks at minimal additive loading while remaining susceptible to rapid disruption during atomization. However, the multiscale relationships linking molecular design, supramolecular organization, rheology, and atomization remain poorly understood.

title: Protein Language Model-Boosted Prediction of Isoelectric Point
abstract: pH plays a key role in many biological processes. When the solution pH equals the isoelectric point (pI) of a protein, the protein carries zero net charge, which minimizes its solubility and thus promotes aggregation. Here we present ESMpI, a sequence-based protein pI predictor that combines optimized pKa values of seven ionizable residue types and two terminals with embeddings from a pre-trained protein language model.

title: Mathematical Modeling of Coupled Electronic and Ionic Transport Mechanics in Flow-Electrode Capacitive Deionization
abstract: Flow Capacitive Deionization (FCDI) is an electrochemical ion removal technology well-suited for continuous desalination of brackish waters, as well as ion-specific removal. Despite over a decade of research into FCDI, few researchers have probed the transient and spatially dependent mechanisms of ion transport and electro-adsorption within flow electrodes. In this study, transport equations describing the advection of overpotential along with the flowing electrode are coupled with the Nernst-Planck equations governing ion transport within the ion exchange membranes, water channel, and slurry…

title: A Stereochemical Blueprint for Thermoresponsive Polymers
abstract: Predicting polymer structure-property relationships is challenging due to the vast chemical expanse of polymer design space and the limited availability of high-quality datasets that effectively span the design space. Here, we present a physics-informed framework that integrates high-throughput molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with machine learning to predict the lower critical solution temperature (LCST) of stereochemically diverse poly(Nisopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) systems using 5632 MD simulation trajectories, corresponding to a cumulative simulation time of 2816 µs.

title: Discovery of new octadecanoids in γ-linolenic acid rich oils
abstract: 17 novel hydroxy fatty acids derived from LA, ALA, and GLA were characterized in evening 2 primrose, borage and hemp oil. Structural characterization was based on semi-synthetic 3 standards generated by autoxidation, photoxidation and enzymatic conversions, combined 4 with LC-MS and GC-MS analysis with multiple derivatization strategies. Novel oxylipins 6-5 HODE and 7-HODE, presumably formed as site-products of Δ6-desaturase, showed 6 characteristic patterns in GLA-rich oils: 6-HODE occurred at high levels in in evening primrose 7 oil (23 ± 1 mg/100 g) and in borage oil (84 ± 7 mg/100 g)…

title: Accuracy in Homonuclear Distance Determinations by Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy: The Benefits of Fast Magic-Angle Spinning up to 100 kHz
abstract: Homonuclear distance measurements by solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy under magic-angle spinning (MAS) conditions are key to structural analysis in complex materials. While a wide variety of dipolar recoupling techniques involving the excitation of double quantum (DQ) coherences is available, the excitation efficiency is critically affected by the chemical-shift anisotropy (CSA) and the (often unknown) relative orientations between chemical-shift and dipolar-coupling tensors of the involved nuclei.

title: Solving density-of-states occupation in disordered systems using neural networks
abstract: Describing density-of-states occupation with high precision in disordered systems is crucial for modeling charge transport and understanding doping mechanisms or interfacial energy-level alignment. Beyond fundamental insight from a mechanistic understanding of these physical phenomena, accurate modeling is pivotal for optimizing technological applications in optoelectronic and thermoelectric devices. However, the required calculations are computationally demanding and inherently complex, preventing systematic computational-experimental approaches.

title: d10 Coinage Metal Organic Chalcogenolates: Tuning Dimensionality and Properties through Phenylthiolate Functionalization
abstract: Metal–Organic Chalcogenolates (MOCs) based on d 10 coinage metals constitute a versatile class of coordination polymers combining anisotropic structures with diverse functional properties. In this review, we examine a series of 23 Cu(I), Ag(I), and Au(I)-based MOCs obtained from eight functionalized thiophenolate ligands. The systematic comparison of these compounds highlights how the metal identity, ligand functionalization, steric hindrance, and secondary interactions govern the coordination modes and, most importantly, the dimensionality of the resulting networks.

title: Mechanochemical Activation of Strontium for the Selective Cross-Coupling of Chlorosilanes
abstract: Silicon-containing compounds are important in both academic and industrial settings, and the reductive coupling of chlorosilanes is a widely used approach for the formation of Si–Si bonds. However, despite its long history, this strategy for the formation of Si–Si bonds has remained largely limited to homocoupling, while a general synthetic method for selective heterocoupling has yet to be established. Previous strategies have relied on the stepwise generation of silicon nucleophiles or electrochemical methods.

title: Peptide-Directed Ligand Design Enables Chemical Disruption of the Nrf2/MafG Coiled-Coil Transcription Factor Complex.
abstract: Transcription factor protein interactions remain among the most challenging targets in chemical biology, particularly those driven by leucine zipper coiled coil assemblies. For this challenge we developed a peptide-directed ligand design strategy identifying inhibitors of the Nrf2/MafG transcription factor complex, a key driver of cytoprotective signalling and cancer chemoresistance. MafG-derived α-helical peptides bind Nrf2 and disrupt formation of the Nrf2/MafG/DNA complex.

title: A Fragment-Based Mechanistic Potential for Noncovalent Systems: Combining Conceptual DFT and Quantum Chemical Topology Domains
abstract: Within a framework combining conceptual Density Functional Theory (cDFT) with the computational efficiency of the quantum chemical topology (QCT) description of matter, we introduce a mechanistic potential designed for the fast exploration of intermolecular potential-energy surfaces between rigid molecular fragments. The proposed strategy deliberately retains only a minimal set of physically interpretable contributions, namely electrostatics, charge transfer, and dispersion.

title: Directional Control of Droplet Motion via Geometric Gating
abstract: We explore new methods for inducing the movement of water droplets on elastomeric substrates, such as polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). Our approach builds upon the well-known phenomenon that water droplets move easily across these substrates when swelled with silicone oil. While designing shallow open channels and traps on a PDMS film offers a simple way to control a droplet's trajectory by tilting the substrate in two orthogonal directions, this method is poorly suited for manipulating multiple droplets simultaneously. To address this limitation, we introduce two new methods.

title: Nucleus-Independent Chemical Shifts in disordered nanoporous carbons are governed by the long-range magnetic response of the carbon framework
abstract: Nanoporous carbons are widely used in energy storage, gas storage, and separation technologies due to their high surface area, porosity, and electrical conductivity. Understanding atomic-scale structure is critical for interpreting performance, yet disorder greatly complicates characterization. NMR chemical shifts of adsorbed molecules have emerged as a probe of structural disorder, but how nucleus-independent chemical shifts (NICS) relate to structure in realistic, disordered carbons remains poorly understood.

title: DeMiR: Density-Matrix-Informed Representations for Molecular Property Prediction
abstract: The Hohenberg–Kohn theorem, which states that all physical quantities in the ground state are functionals of the electron density, suggests that much of a molecule's behavior is encoded in its electronic structure. This study proposes DeMiR, a model that treats electron density matrix prediction as a pretraining task. DeMiR reconstructs cc-pVDZ/B3LYP density matrices for molecules ranging in size from QM9-scale molecules to drug-like molecules with up to 146 atoms, achieving median NMAE values of 1.0% and 2.16%, respectively.

title: Carboxyl–Group Removal and Return: Mechanistic and Strategic Advances in Decarboxylation–Carboxylation
abstract: Carboxylic acids are ubiquitous functionalities and indispensable synthetic linchpins in organic chemistry. In recent years, strategies involving the removal, exchange, or recycling of the carboxyl group, particularly decarboxylation and carboxylation have gained remarkable momentum, partly driven by the imperative to valorize carbon dioxide generated in chemical transformations. Beyond simple CO2 extrusion, tandem decarboxylation–carboxylation and related cyclic processes have emerged as powerful yet underexplored approaches for constructing carboxylic acids in a single operation.

title: Resolving Kinase Resistance Landscapes via Antisymmetric Siamese Graph Networks and Co-Folding Ensembles
abstract: Acquired clinical resistance to small-molecule kinase inhibitors arising from single-point mutations within the ATP-binding cleft presents a critical challenge in precision oncology. Conventional computational modeling relies either on rigid docking—which overlooks induced structural alterations—or computationally demanding alchemical free energy perturbation (FEP) methods that cannot scale across wide mutational panels.

title: Hybrid Organosilicon Polymers Integrating Latent Si–Si Chromophores and Orthogonal Si–O–C Reactivity
Minimum Knowledge Collaboration enables joint materials development through protected optimization
abstract: Materials companies must jointly develop products that meet competing requirements while keeping their formulations, processes and models private. Sample exchange alone can leave their searches poorly coordinated. We introduce Minimum Knowledge Collaboration (MKC), which connects private Bayesian optimizers through bounded candidate descriptions and company-specific search directions. Mathematical analysis links representation error, feasible private responses and information-limited search.

title: Electrochemically Controlled Crystallization Using Selective Bipolar Membrane Electrodialysis
abstract: Nitrogen and phosphorus nutrient recovery from wastewater represents a critical frontier for circular fertilizer manufacturing and effective water treatment. Conventional chemical precipitation remains hindered by the need for expensive reagent consumables. Here, we examine an integrated, chemical-free electrochemical mixer (ECM) system that leverages selective bipolar membrane electrodialysis (SBED) to achieve precise struvite (MgNH4PO4 · 6H2O) crystallization.

title: Transition-State Steric Fields Capture Geometric Signatures Associated with Electronic Perturbations in Asymmetric Catalysis
abstract: In data analysis of molecular catalysis, molecular shape can be represented by voxel descriptors generated by mapping molecular structures onto a three-dimensional grid according to atomic van der Waals radii. Such voxel representations of molecular shape can be treated as steric molecular fields and are generally used as steric descriptors. However, because electronic perturbations can lead to systematic changes in molecular geometry, steric fields constructed from transition-state (TS) structures may also capture geometric signatures.

title: Polymorph Influence on Sequential Anion Exchange Doping and Charge Transport in Poly(didodecyl-quaterthiophene) (PQT) for Organic Thermoelectrics
Plasmonic Coupling Within Atomically Precise Nanocluster Dimers for Engineering Hot-Carrier Generation and Molecular Activation
abstract: Activating the exceptionally strong N≡N remains a fundamental challenge due to the chemical inertness of molecular nitrogen (N2). Plasmonic nanoclusters offer a promising approach by generating localized electromagnetic fields and energetic hot carriers that can drive bond activation at ambient conditions. Here, we combine real-time time-dependent density functional theory with Ehrenfest molecular dynamics to reveal how plasmonic coupling between tetrahedral Ag20 nanoclusters governs N2 activation and dissociation.
authors: Sharma S. R. K. C. Yamijala

title: From Rotor to Motor: Dissecting Design Principles for Light-Driven Directional Motion
abstract: Research on molecular motors continues to expand as increasing attention is devoted to dynamic and out-of-equilibrium chemical systems. Among the different classes of artificial molecular machines, light-driven motors are the most extensively present, yet the fundamental principles governing their directional motion remain difficult to disentangle, particularly for non-specialists.

title: Harnessing π-d magnetic interactions in Co porphyrins by metal-ligand coordination
abstract: π-Multiradicalic compounds fabricated by on-surface synthesis have emerged as a powerful platform to interrogate spin interactions at the atomic scale. However, the introduction and role of unpaired d-electrons on such systems, and the study of π-d electronic interactions, are still incipient. In this context, a crucial point is the tunability of the inherent magnetic properties of such π-d architectures by incorporation of peripheral metal-organic coordination, which at the same time allows creating self-assembled architectures.

title: A robust multiwell workflow for quantitative and nontargeted chemical exposomics at cohort scale
abstract: Chemical exposomics enables comprehensive profiling of environmental substances and their metabolic perturbations, providing new opportunities to uncover environmental drivers of disease. To realize its full potential in human exposome initiatives, more reproducible high-throughput workflows are needed that combine sensitive quantitative targeted analysis with nontargeted molecular discovery in small serum volumes.

title: Ultra-Low CoNi Alloy Nanoparticle Loaded Polypyrrole Nanospheres as Oxygen Electrocatalysts in Alkaline to Near-Neutral Zinc-Air Batteries
abstract: Dearth of a wide-range pH-adaptable bifunctional oxygen electrocatalyst is a bottleneck in the advancement of efficient metal-air batteries as catalysts optimized for alkaline media often lose effectiveness under near-neutral conditions. Herein, we report an ultralow (~1 atomic%) amount of CoNi alloy loaded polypyrrole-derived graphitic nanoparticle (CoNiPpy) system as a pH-adaptable oxygen electrocatalyst for high energy density and durability in near-neutral zinc-air batteries (ZABs) with 100% coulombic efficiency.

title: Surface hydroxyls act as key intermediates in the selective oxidative dehydrogenation of 2-propanol on Co3O4
abstract: Transition-metal oxides typically catalyze aerobic oxidation reactions with high activity even at low temperatures, but rarely with high selectivity. Owing to the complexity of competing surface processes on such catalysts, the rational design of selective low-temperature catalysts still requires a deeper mechanistic understanding of the active surface and reaction intermediates.

title: Selective Operando Visualization of Ultrathin Lithium in Li-Metal Batteries by Neutron Capture Imaging
abstract: Operando visualization of ultrathin lithium is essential for understanding plating and stripping in lithium-metal batteries, but existing neutron imaging techniques lack sufficient sensitivity for ultra-thin lithium layers formed at crucial early stages. Here we introduce neutron capture imaging (NCI), which selectively detects tritons generated by neutron capture in 6 Li. Ex situ measurements of electrochemically plated and thermally evaporated 6 Li demonstrate sensitivity around 10 nm for a 1.5 h acquisition and two-dimensional imaging with around 100 μm lateral resolution.

title: Mousanes: Convergent Synthesis and Diversification of Serially Spiro-Fused Cyclobutanes
abstract: Connecting cyclobutanes through successive spiro junctions offers a way to restrict the relative positions and orientations of functional groups along a saturated framework. Here we describe a convergent synthesis of mousanes, dispirodecane scaffolds comprising three cyclobutanes. A functionalized methylenecyclobutene is prepared on decagram scale by elimination of an iodo-bicyclo[1.1.1]pentanederived precursor. This 1,3-diene undergoes regioselective, triplet-sensitized [2+2] homodimerization to construct the central cyclobutane and both spiro junctions.

title: Hypoboric Acid Catecholate (HAC) Catalysis for Stereoselective Decarboxylative Borylation of Redox-Active Esters
abstract: The Hypoboric Acid Catecholate (HAC) is a new class of diboron reagent bearing a borylcatecholato and a boronic acid moiety. Herein, we demonstrate that HACs can also be expontaneously formed in situ from collections of catechols and hypoboric acid. These HACs catalyze the decarboxylative borylation of redox-active esters, providing superior reactivity and selectivity. Equilibrium and kinetic NMR experiments indicate that the catalytic turnover is enabled by the high affinity of catechols for hypoboric acid and their low affinity for boronic acids that is uncovered herein.

title: Glycine specifically labelled proteins to enhance solution NMR of methylene groups
abstract: Specific isotopic labelling of proteins has greatly advanced biomolecular NMR. Protein domains, individual residues or certain chemical groups with specific patterns of isotopes can be incorporated to optimize the use of NMR pulse schemes. Here, we describe a novel cell-free protein expression protocol that allows specific isotopic labelling of glycine residues, whilst all other amino acids are independently labelled.

title: Computational assessment of a proposed Na+/Ag+ ion-exchange route to Ag2MgSiO4, a predicted wurtzite-derived silver silicate
abstract: Low-temperature ion exchange can provide a route to metastable inorganic compounds that are not favoured by equilibrium synthesis. We assess the proposed preparation of Ag2MgSiO4 from Na2MgSiO4 in molten AgNO3, using exchange energies, reported preparation controls and lattice-dynamical calculations. MLIP screening agrees in sign with the selected published DFT references, but the reaction set is linked by reciprocal reactions and thermodynamic cycles and is not an independent sample of synthesis outcomes.

title: Photocatalytic performance of silver clusters on anatase TiO2 for bisphenol A degradation in water under solar light
abstract: The increasing occurrence of bisphenol A (BPA) in water sources raises significant environmental and health concerns, demanding efficient and sustainable remediation strategies. In this work, we investigate the photocatalytic degradation of BPA using silver metal clusters (Ag5) supported on anatase TiO2 under simulated solar irradiation. The deposition of Ag5 clusters significantly enhances visible-light absorption, promotes charge separation and improves photocatalytic performance, achieving an apparent rate constant (kobs) of 0.0142 min-1, corresponding to a ~43% improvement compared to…

title: Structure-Based Design of Potent Pan-YTHDF Ligands
abstract: N6-Adenosine methylation (m6A) is the most abundant post-transcriptional modification of mRNA. The reader proteins YTHDF1, YTHDF2, and YTHDF3 recognize m6A-RNA in the cytosol. Here, we present a protein structurebased medicinal chemistry campaign that resulted in the pan-YTHDF inhibitor 34, which shows for YTHDF2 an equilibrium dissociation constant (Kd) of 0.14 µM determined by calorimetry. Compound 34 binds the three YTHDF paralogs with comparable affinity, while being selective against YTHDC1 and YTHDC2.

title: Stacking Interactions of Druglike Heterocycles with Histidine
abstract: Histidine side chains are prevalent in binding sites and can engage in stacking interactions with heterocyclic ligand components. However, efforts to harness these interactions for molecular recognition are often hampered by an incomplete understanding of the factors that control the strength and preferred geometries of these interactions. To this end, we provide a comprehensive computational analysis of stacked dimers of druglike heterocycles with the three protomers of the histidine side chain.

title: bioRheoFlow A Rheometric Platform for In Situ Biofilm Mechanics Under Controlled Flow Conditions
abstract: Biofilm mechanics depend strongly on growth history, hydration, nutrient availability, and interfacial attachment, yet conventional rheology requires harvesting and transfer that can perturb the as-grown structure. Here, we introduce bioRheoFlow, a 3D-printed rheometer-mounted platform for cultivation and mechanical characterization without sample transfer. The platform combines evaporation compensation with static or axial nutrient flow, and benchmark measurements validate its rheometric performance.

title: Optogenetics researchers win Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine
abstract: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann, and Georg Nagel receive the prize for their work on light-gated ion channels and optogenetics

title: A Robust π-Conjugated Radical Cocrystal
Integrating transcriptomic analysis to explore biomarkers and therapeutic targets for rheumatoid arthritis: a case-control and systems biology approach
abstract: BackgroundRheumatoid Arthritis (RA) is a highly variable and unpredictable autoimmune disease, relying solely on physical symptoms often leads to delayed treatment and irreversible joint destruction. Therefore, identifying biomarkers in RA is necessary to bridge the gap between a patient's unique biological profile and successful clinical management. This study aims to identify distinct molecular signatures in RA patients by integrating systems biology and case-control methodologies.MethodsTranscriptomic datasets from various sources specifically synovial tissues, macrophages, blood, T-cells, natural killer T-cells, natural killer cells, neutrophils, and monocytes were analysed. Differentially Expressed Genes and functional enrichment pathways were identified, followed by Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis to pinpoint hub genes. Machine learning models were used to extract consensus biomarkers. Two of the predicted biomarkers IL2RG) and Interferon-Gamma (IFNG) were further validated using an Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) in RA patient serum samples.ResultsThe analysis revealed that synovial tissues and synovial macrophages exhibited pronounced transcriptomic expression changes. Six consensus biomarkers such as IFNG, PTEN, IL2RG, CDKN2D, VEGFA, and CDKN1A were computationally prioritized in synovial macrophages. Among these, IL2RG and IFNG were selected for preliminary experimental validation by ELISA. IL2RG concentrations were significantly higher in RA patients (1.34 ± 0.11 ng/mL) than in healthy controls (0.83 ± 0.07 ng/mL), while IFNG levels showed only a marginal increase (1.91 ± 0.06 pg/mL) compared to controls (1.69 ± 0.06 pg/mL).ConclusionBy integrating multi-tissue transcriptomic profiling with machine learning, this study mapped critical molecular changes in RA and prioritized six consensus biomarkers within synovial macrophages. Experimental validation confirmed that IL2RG and IFNG are significantly elevated in RA patients compared to healthy controls. These findings offer a promising, minimally invasive molecular markers for diagnosis and personalized clinical management in RA.

title: The Oxacyclobutylidenecarbene-Oxacyclopentyne System: Experimental Access and Theoretical Studies
abstract: Photolysis of 3-(1a,9b-dihydro-1H-cyclopropa[l]phenanthren-1-ylidene)oxetane in benzene generates the putative 3-oxacyclobutylidenecarbene, which rearranges into 3-oxacyclopentyne, the smallest heterocyclic alkyne reported to date that is comprised entirely of second-row elements in the ring. This strained heterocyclic alkyne could be intercepted as a [4 + 2] adduct with a cyclopentadienone derivative that subsequently loses CO to form a phthalan core, a heterocyclic motif that is found in many biologically active natural products, pharmaceuticals, and advanced materials. Calculations at the FIC-NEVPT2/def2-TZVPP//CASSCF[8,8]/def2-TZVPP level of theory, incorporating a CPCM model for benzene, show that singlet 3-oxacyclobutylidenecarbene lies well below the triplet (ΔE = −42.8 kcal/mol) and has to surmount a free energy barrier of 7.80 kcal/mol to ring expand into 3-oxacyclopentyne. The ring expansion of singlet carbene to the cycloalkyne was calculated to be essentially thermoneutral with ΔGrxn° estimated to be +0.68 kcal/mol. The gas phase calculated geometry of 3-oxacyclopentyne reveals a molecule with C2v symmetry and extremely distorted bond angles of 112.2° at each of the two carbons involved in the triple bond. The triple bond itself is more typical with a calculated bond length of 1.24 Å. The gas phase electronic strain energy (ΔESE) of 3-oxacyclopentyne, computed via a homodesmotic scheme, was estimated to be 70.1 kcal/mol.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Torque-optimized body morphing enables rapid surface to underwater diving in whirligig beetles
abstract: Known for their rapid water surface locomotion, whirligig beetles (Gyrinidae) are also fast divers. They can transition from the surface to underwater swimming in under 100 ms. Diving requires them to generate sufficient hydrodynamic torque to break the water surface and reorient the body. However, the mechanism by which whirligigs create the necessary pitch-down torque is unknown. Here, we show that their diving is achieved by bending the abdomen. The inertial hydrodynamic pressure on the flexed abdomen generates the torque necessary for surface breaking and body rotation.

title: Metabolic cost sets the shear stress profile of optimal vascular trees
abstract: Vascular remodeling responds to local wall shear stress, but transport efficiency belongs to the network as a whole. We connect these scales by minimizing dissipation under a fixed maintenance budget, with vessel cost proportional to mass raised to an exponent b. At an optimum, dissipated power is proportional to vessel cost. This yields the shear set point |{tau} | {propto} r^(b-1){ell}^(b-1)/2 for radius r and length {ell}, with uniform shear recovered at b = 1. The associated local adaptation rule decreases the global functional, although the topology it reaches retains a memory of development. Simulations with 400 and 700 sinks show that staged growth improves transport mainly by allowing pruned connections to regrow. Fluctuating demand sustains loops without increasing the maintenance budget. The local condition fixes allocation on a given support, whereas growth and variable demand shape the topology that survives.

title: Electrode-Tethered DNA: Interfacial Mechanics and Switching Dynamics from Ensemble-Level Atomistic Simulations
abstract: Surface-tethered DNA, anchored to gold by the late 1990s, has matured into a versatile platform for biosensing, computing and actuation. Whereas the molecular behavior of DNA in bulk solution is well characterized, that of DNA at electrode interfaces remains far less understood. Here we investigate the mechanics and dynamics of electrode-tethered double-stranded DNA across surface chemistries, salt concentrations and applied potentials. Using GPU-accelerated all-atom molecular dynamics, we sample trajectory ensembles totaling 144 s over 620 simulations. The simulations reproduce key experimental observations yet uncover molecular behavior that had gone unnoticed despite nearly three decades of research. Ensemble statistics reveal a preferred orientation about the helical axis upon surface contact. Energetic analysis identifies a substantial role for Onsager-Samaras-type repulsion in opposing that contact. By reproducing experimental trends while resolving their molecular origins, these ensembles substantially narrow the longstanding simulation-experiment gap and provide a basis for engineering tethered-DNA devices.

title: Snail shell-derived hydroxyapatite on ant clay: a sustainable solution for phosphate sequestration and circular agricultural reuse
abstract: In this study, a sustainable adsorbent comprising hydroxyapatite derived from snail shells and clay collected from ant nests was developed and used for the efficient removal of phosphate (PO4 3-) from aqueous solutions. The synthesized adsorbent was characterized using different characterization techniques like FTIR spectroscopy, XRD, SEM, TGA, PZC, and BET analysis to confirm its successful synthesis, morphology, thermal stability, surface charges, and surface area, respectively. The adsorbent was systematically investigated for phosphate adsorption by optimizing key experimental parameters, comprising contact time (25 min), adsorbent dosage (25 mg), initial phosphate concentration (5 mg L-1), solution pH (5), and temperature (40 °C). Furthermore, the adsorption kinetics followed the pseudo-second-order model (R 2 = 0.98), implying that the adsorption rate was controlled by the availability of active sites. The equilibrium data were best fitted to the Langmuir isotherm model (R 2 = 0.98), with the maximum adsorption capacity of 97.18 mg g-1. The thermodynamic analysis confirmed the endothermic (ΔH° > 0) and spontaneous (ΔG° 4 3-. Exploratory machine-learning modelling of 84 experimental observations showed that SVR-RBF most accurately predicted phosphate-removal efficiency (cross-validated R 2 = 0.789 ± 0.127), while Extra Trees regression provided the strongest prediction of adsorption capacity (cross-validated R 2 = 0.894 ± 0.210). The modelled response trends were consistent with the experimentally identified optimum conditions, supporting the use of data-driven methods for adsorption-process interpretation and future optimization. Additionally, the PO4 3--loaded adsorbent was evaluated as a fertilizer for wheat cultivation; it induced an enhanced growth performance compared to pristine ant clay, highlighting its potential for sustainable agricultural applications. Thus, this study established the adsorbent's efficacy in PO4 3- removal and its suitability for improving growth parameters, including germination rate, shoot/root development, and chlorophyll/protein content, resulting in improved phosphorus bioavailability.

title: From Benchmark to Bench: Can Agents Survive Real-World Drug Discovery?
abstract: Agentic systems increasingly coordinate molecular-design tools, but it is unclear which layer of the stack limits outcomes on real projects. We developed MAGI, an open modular agent that authors objectives, launches and monitors optimization, interprets structure--activity relationships, and revises its strategy accordingly. MAGI generates molecules either directly through the LLM or by delegating to REINVENT 4, with scoring services interchangeable behind a common contract. We tested it across nine retrospective lead-optimization campaigns from three pharmaceutical companies, replayed under fixed temporal cutoffs. Both routes produced valid structures: LLM proposals stayed closer to local chemistry and reached comparable or higher primary activity in fewer operations, whereas REINVENT explored broader chemical space. Whether a campaign met its objective depended on the predictive models, not on the generation route: attainment followed model accuracy on the chemistry proposed, dropping once that chemistry moved outside the model's applicability domain. Separately, a blinded evaluation asked whether the MAGI's output could pass as expert work: chemists were not able to discriminate agentic proposals from held-out compounds, and judged the SAR reasoning broadly plausible yet incomplete. Together, these results position MAGI as a coordination layer pluggable into existing computational chemistry workflows. The ceiling on real projects, however, remains currently set by scorer applicability rather than by tool orchestration.

title: Efficient Secure Federated Learning via Information-Theoretically Secure Key Distribution: A Medical Imaging Case Study
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) enables collaborative training of models across institutions without centralizing sensitive data, making it well-suited for privacy-concerned applications, such as medical imaging. To protect FL model updates during secure aggregation, additive masking is commonly employed. However, its underlying classical key establishment is only computationally secure. On the other hand, physics-based Information-Theoretically Secure (ITS) key exchange introduces practical constraints: finite key generation rates and time-limited storage severely limit throughput and sustained training of uncompressed models. In this work, we address this bottleneck by developing an FL framework that integrates frozen backbones, knowledge distillation, and quantization. These techniques reduce communication payload and, consequently, key material consumption. Moving beyond simulation, we benchmark this framework on a real physics-based key distribution testbed involving a chest X-ray classification application. Our results show that key usage can be reduced by $\sim$35$\times$ while maintaining predictive accuracy. This prevents buffer depletion and key expiration, enabling sustainable FL training under physical key generation constraints.

title: Valid Stopping in Adaptive Generator-Verifier Loops
abstract: Numerous agentic workflows are based on a generator-verifier loop: a generator proposes candidates, a cheap verifier scores them, and the workflow terminates when a proposal is verified as good enough. The verifier typically proxies a more costly ground-truth oracle, and as the generator searches adaptively against it, false acceptances may accumulate. Proposals can pass the proxy but fail under the costlier ground-truth check. We study when to stop these loops while controlling the false discovery rate of the accepted proposals. Our construction introduces tools of independent interest in distribution-free statistical testing and conformal risk control, including analysis of $e$-values constructed through index betting and a novel conformal risk control procedure for non-monotone losses. We validate the approach in synthetic settings and on a protein-design benchmark.

title: ARO: Aligned Representation learning for multi-Omics data
abstract: The high cost of functional molecular assays, and prevalence of missing modalities and unmatched samples in computational biology, create significant barriers to comprehensive multi-omic profiling, essential for capturing and reasoning over molecules, cells, tissues, and organisms. This work proposes a model that learns meaningful representations from multi-omics cancer data supporting the reconstruction of missing and unpaired modalities. Contrary to increasingly complex, larger models, e.g. Foundation Models (FMs), ARO prioritizes practical applicability in limited or incomplete data settings. ARO optimally reconstructs missing modalities (MSE of $0.15$ on the validation and test data in the Unmasked settings), with its learned latent embeddings enabling a downstream cancer classification task. Our findings indicate that analyzing diverse molecular layers as a single integrated system offers a reliable and cost-efficient approach, reducing dependence on large-scale experimental testing, while still supporting multi-omic exploration in limited data settings.

title: Exact vortex decomposition of the shift current
abstract: Does any integer survive in the shift current, and does the Chern number control its sign? We show that the shift vector is a singular field on the Brillouin torus. Its curl has two sources: the interband Berry curvature and quantised point charges at the zeros of the transition dipole. Inverting this relation gives an exact decomposition of the shift conductivity, valid at every frequency, into one sector linear in the integer charges and three continuous sectors. As a testing ground, we take a graphene-Haldane bilayer: a model that lets us sweep the interband Chern number through five values at fixed gap to isolate its role. We also test the formalism against the time-reversal-symmetric biased AB bilayer. Whenever a charge sits at the band edge, and trigonal warping is present, the integer sector alone accounts for the band-edge peak. The relevant integer is not the Chern number but the winding of that single charge. Its sign, combined with a valley-dependent profile, sets the sign of the photocurrent. In these bilayers, sign reversals across topological transitions follow this winding; the invariant changes with it only when the same gap closing does both. A band-edge charge needs no invariant. It only requires that the two band-edge sublattices not be connected by the nearest-neighbour hopping, and trigonal warping makes it visible.

title: Latent Flow Matching for Molecular Graph Generation
abstract: Modern graph generative models typically operate directly in the discrete graph space, explicitly generating node and edge variables, which can become costly as graphs grow. In this paper, we perform generation explicitly on latent representations of entire graphs obtained from a pretrained Variational Autoencoder with high reconstruction fidelity. The generated representations, obtained through flow matching, are then decoded only at the final step. Across molecular benchmarks of increasing size, our approach achieves strong validity and FCD while offering a favorable quality-efficiency trade-off compared with state-of-the-art explicit graph generative models. One of the main advantages of this formulation is that the graph representation only needs to be learned once, after which the same one can be reused across multiple generative objectives without retraining. We demonstrate generation guided by molecular properties and further introduce validity-aware generation though a classifier learned directly in latent space. All code will be made available upon acceptance.

title: Quantum spectral thermodynamics and active learning enable million-scale exploration of high-entropy ceramics
abstract: Understanding phase stability and navigating vast compositional spaces in multicomponent solids remain central challenges in solid-state chemistry. Here, we develop a quantum spectral thermodynamic framework connecting interaction-induced phonon spectral broadening to free energy, alongside an uncertainty-guided active-learning workflow that explores 7.7 million high-entropy ceramic configurations at density-functional-theory fidelity, achieving a $10^5$-fold acceleration. We show that phonon self-energy effects arising from chemical disorder provide an intrinsic vibrational contribution to thermodynamic stabilization beyond ideal configurational entropy, compensating unfavorable mixing enthalpies and suppressing phase separation. Across the chemical space, we uncover a robust ~12 at.% solute threshold separating strengthening and softening regimes, associated with the filling of metal-carbon antibonding states. Chemical disorder further enables an unusual combination of high-temperature mechanical stiffness and low thermal conductivity, together with anomalous temperature-dependent lattice heat transport. This work establishes a quantum spectral foundation for connecting many-body interactions to thermodynamics and phase stability, while providing a scalable framework for exploring previously inaccessible multicomponent chemical spaces.

title: Bad Loans, Good Governance: Thresholds, Spillovers, and the New Econometrics of Non-Performing Loans in EU
abstract: This paper synthesises and extends the empirical literature on bank non-performing loans (NPLs), moving from classical macroeconomic and bank-level explanations to the 2026 research frontier of non-linear thresholds, spatial network externalities, explainable machine learning, ESG governance, and climate-risk channels. The central argument is that NPLs are not merely the product of bad luck or adverse macroeconomic cycles. They are regime-dependent outcomes shaped jointly by institutional depth, currency exposure, spatial connectedness, bank behaviour, risk culture, and governance quality.

title: Mapping Functional Transitions across Protein Homologues from a Single Simulation: Application of gEDES-HM to Adenylate Kinases
abstract: Proteins fluctuate across different conformational states, which constitute a dynamic ensemble that regulates their interaction networks and functions. Predicting the conformational landscape remains a computational challenge, and even more difficult is capturing the link between state distributions and specific functions within protein homologues. Here, we present gEDES-HM (generalized Ensemble Docking with Enhanced sampling of pocket Shape-Homology Modeling), a scalable computational protocol enabling us to remap conformational ensembles obtained from enhanced sampling simulations of a single protein to its homologous family members, removing the need to perform individual simulations for all of them and thus speeding up the whole process by orders of magnitude. Specifically, we exploit our recent gEDES protocol to bias through metadynamics simulations the shape and volume of the binding site(s) of a reference protein. Next, a number of maximally diverse conformations of the protein are extracted from a multistep cluster analysis and used together as a multitemplate library for comparative modeling of the conformational ensemble of each homologue in the pool. This enables the functional conformational ensemble of one protein to be transferred to its homologues and used, for example, in restrained ensemble docking. We validated the protocol on 22 homologues of the E. coli adenylate kinase (hereafter, ADK), corresponding to 26 protein-ligand complexes and spanning 31% to 99% sequence identity to the reference. Our protocol retrieves a bound-like conformation of the protein binding site (corresponding to experimental substrate/inhibitor-bound states) for almost all targets, which allows reproducing native-like binding modes for 92% of the investigated complexes in ensemble docking calculations. Validated so far within a single family, gEDES-HM could provide a practical route to generate binding-competent structural libraries for homologues lacking experimental structures suitable for downstream structure-based modeling.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Iterative computational bioprospecting of hydroxymethylfurfural oxidases combining molecular simulation and machine learning
abstract: The enzymatic oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) is a key step in the sustainable production of polyethylene furanoate (PEF), yet the final oxidation of 5-formyl-2-furancarboxylic acid (FFCA) to FDCA remains the principal bottleneck for industrial application. Although hydroxymethylfurfural oxidases (HMFOs) can catalyze this transformation, naturally occurring enzymes with high FFCA-oxidizing activity remain largely unexplored.

title: Polyglutamine aggregation proceeds by stochastic nucleation in the C. elegans nervous system
abstract: Fibrillar protein aggregation is the hallmark of a wide variety of neurodegenerative diseases. It is still poorly understood how soluble proteins transition to fibrillar aggregates, in particular within the complex environment of cells and tissues. Here, we employ the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of polyglutamine aggregation in the nervous system of a multicellular animal. By using fluorescence microscopy in combination with mathematical modelling, we find that polyglutamine aggregation occurs by stochastic nucleation in individual neurons, at a rate that is of the same order of magnitude as previously determined for muscle cells. The J-protein DNAJB6 strongly suppresses polyglutamine aggregation in both tissues, consistent with a mechanism in which aggregation is limited by primary nucleation. We confirm that the same mechanism holds true for a construct including the disease-relevant flanking regions of Huntingtin exon 1. Altogether, our data reveal that polyglutamine aggregation occurs spontaneously and largely independent of the cellular context.

title: Optimizing the Optimizer: Language Models Discover Faster Molecular Relaxation Algorithms
abstract: Geometry optimization is a major cost in many quantum-chemical workflows: each optimization step requires one force evaluation, and at the density-functional level that evaluation dominates the wall time. Research in this area has produced a broad range of optimization methods, and we ask whether a language model can improve on the best of them through autoresearch. An agent rewrites the optimizer itself to minimize force-call counts, restrained by two admission gates that reject premature stopping and improvements that do not generalize to unseen molecules. Starting from Sella, the fastest open-source optimizer available, the search produces AutoSella, a family of two optimizers. Both of them deliver consistent force-call reductions relative to Sella across held-out molecular benchmarks and potentials not used during the search. Most notably, at the r2SCAN-3c DFT level, the best variant requires only 40.2-77.2% of Sella's force calls while achieving the same energy reduction, even though agent used no DFT gradients.

title: Dynamical Valence Fluctuations and Magnetic Anisotropy in Sm(Co,Cu)$_5$
abstract: The magnetic properties of Sm-based intermetallics are governed by a delicate interplay between localized $4f$ states, exchange interactions, and valence fluctuations, yet the role of dynamical $4f$ correlations remains poorly understood. Here we investigate the electronic structure and magnetic anisotropy of SmCo$_5$ and SmCu$_5$ using self-consistent DFT+$U$(ED), which explicitly treats dynamical fluctuations of the Sm $4f$ shell. We find that SmCo$_5$ exhibits pronounced Sm$^{2+}$--Sm$^{3+}$ valence fluctuations, with the $4f$ ground state dominated by $f^5$ and $f^6$ configurations. The resulting dynamical $4f$ correlations yield near compensation of the Sm spin and orbital moments and provide a quantitative description of the electronic structure, magnetic moments, and large uniaxial magnetic anisotropy of SmCo$_5$. Upon replacing Co with Cu, the balance shifts toward the $f^6$ configuration, with substantial changes in the Sm spin and orbital moments. In SmCu$_5$, this evolution of the $4f$ configuration is accompanied by a pronounced reduction of both the total magnetic moment and magnetic anisotropy. These results demonstrate that dynamical $4f$ valence fluctuations are essential for understanding the contrasting magnetic properties of SmCo$_5$ and SmCu$_5$ and provide a microscopic framework for describing magnetic anisotropy upon Co to Cu substitution in Sm(Co,Cu)$_5$.

title: AI in Fixed Prosthodontics: A Bibliometric and AI-Assisted Qualitative Analysis of Research Trends and Translational Gaps (2011-2026)
abstract: BackgroundA comprehensive understanding of the global research trends and translational gaps in AI for fixed prosthodontics remains limited. This study aimed to characterize research trends, delineate thematic clusters, and identify translational gaps in AI for fixed prosthodontics using an integrated bibliometric and AI-assisted qualitative synthesis framework.MethodsA bibliometric analysis was conducted using the Web of Science Core Collection (2011-2026). A total of 519 records were retrieved and manually screened, yielding 377 eligible publications for quantitative analysis.

title: Causality-integrated graph learning for multi-endpoint toxicity prediction
